agp.title: Ambulatory Glucose Profile
agp.summary: Your readings from 14 days, shown as one typical day.

transcript.heading: The 24-hour glucose pattern
notes: The blue line is your median: the middle reading at each hour, over 14 days.
Your median is highest at 9am: 169 mg/dL, after breakfast.
The shaded bands show how much your days differ. At 2pm they are widest: from 80 to 276 mg/dL.

transcript.heading: Look further back
notes: Is this a real pattern, or two unusual weeks? Open the date range.
Select 30 Days. The calendar marks the days it covers.
Then select Apply Filters. The whole report loads again for 30 days.

transcript.heading: The pattern over 30 days
notes: Over 30 days the shape stays the same: your glucose rises after breakfast and stays high into the afternoon. At 1pm the median is 166 mg/dL.

transcript.heading: Time in range over 30 days
notes: 78% of your readings are in range, 70 to 180 mg/dL. The consensus target is more than 70%.

basal-analysis.title: Basal Rate Analysis
basal-analysis.summary: How your background insulin changes through the day.

transcript.heading: Basal rate by hour
notes: The line is your median basal rate at each hour. Most hours sit between 1.2 and 1.4 U/hr.
At 4pm the median drops to 0.4 U/hr: at this hour your loop often lowers your basal.
Where the shaded bands are wide, the delivered rate changed more at that hour.

transcript.heading: How often your loop changes it
notes: Over 14 days, your loop raised your basal 343 times and lowered it only 93 times.

transcript.heading: Only the latest week
notes: Is this still true now? Open the date range at the top of the report.
Select 7 Days to look at the latest week only.
Then select Apply Filters. The report loads again for those 7 days.

transcript.heading: The last 7 days
notes: In the last 7 days: 161 times higher and 53 times lower. Your loop still raises your basal about three times as often.

battery.title: Battery
battery.summary: How the batteries of your devices charge and run down.

transcript.heading: One card for each device
notes: Each device that sends status reports gets a card. The Trio battery is at 80% now.
In the last 7 days it charged 6 times. After each charge, the battery lasted 16h 30m.

transcript.heading: Look further back
notes: One week shows only a few charges. To see more, change the date range.
Select 30 Days.
Then select Apply Filters.

transcript.heading: Thirty days of charging
notes: Over 30 days the Trio battery charged 29 times, about once a day. Each charge lasted 16h 30m.

transcript.heading: What the longer range shows
notes: The pump battery went as low as 7% in these 30 days.
It was below 30% for 17.3% of the time. In the last 7 days alone, it never went below 53%.

comparison.title: Comparison
comparison.summary: Put two periods side by side, and see what changed.

transcript.heading: Two weeks against two weeks
notes: The report opens on the last 14 days against the 14 days before. Time in range went from 75.9% to 81.1%.

transcript.heading: Choose the periods
notes: To compare other periods, open the presets.
Choose the last 30 days against the 30 days before.

transcript.heading: What changed
notes: The table updates at once. Over 30 days, time in range went from 72.5% to 78.2%.
Your Glycemic Risk Index fell from 37 to 29. A bar to the left means lower, and here lower is better.

transcript.heading: Time in range, side by side
notes: In the earlier 30 days, 72% of your readings were in range.
In the last 30 days, 78% are in range, and the red very high band is smaller.

data-quality.title: Data Quality
data-quality.summary: Find readings that may come from the sensor, not from your glucose.

transcript.heading: Compression lows to review
notes: A compression low is a false low reading when you sleep on the sensor. Possible ones wait here for your review. Now there are none.

transcript.heading: Scan your nights
notes: To scan a night for compression lows, pick its date. Add an end date to scan more nights.
Then select Run Detection. A notice shows how many wait for review.

transcript.heading: Review what it found
notes: It found 1 possible compression low. It now waits here for your review.

transcript.heading: Accept or dismiss
notes: For each one, accept it as a false low, or dismiss it as a real low. Your reports still include these readings.

day-in-review.title: Day in Review
day-in-review.summary: One day in detail: glucose, insulin, carbs and each decision of your pump.

transcript.heading: The day in numbers
notes: 71% of the day's readings are in range. None are low, but 20% are very high.

transcript.heading: Saturday's glucose
notes: You ate 60g of carbs at 6:55am. By 8:45am your glucose was 345 mg/dL.

transcript.heading: Step through the day
notes: The card shows the last decision of the pump, at 10:45am. It forecast 40 mg/dL.
Move the scrubber to any moment. Here, back to the start of the day.
At midnight your glucose was 171 mg/dL. The pump forecast 144 and set 1.40U/hr.

transcript.heading: Another day
notes: To see another day, step back with the arrow.
On Friday, 88.5% of your readings were in range, and 1.2% were low.

ehba1c.title: Estimated HbA1c
ehba1c.summary: What a lab HbA1c test would read, estimated for each day.

transcript.heading: How the estimate works
notes: Each day's estimate uses the average glucose of the 90 days before it. The most recent 30 days count for about half.
Your latest estimate is 6.5%, from Saturday, October 24.

transcript.heading: Your estimate over time
notes: From mid-August it stays between 6.4% and 6.6%.

transcript.heading: Add a lab result
notes: To check the estimate, add a lab HbA1c result. First, enter the date of the blood draw.
Then enter the result in percent, and a note if you want one.
Select Add lab result. The result goes into your list.

transcript.heading: Compare it on the chart
notes: Your lab result shows as a triangle on the chart. On October 10 the lab read 6.8%, and the estimate was 6.6%.

executive-summary.title: Executive Summary
executive-summary.summary: Your most important numbers on one page, for the period you choose.

transcript.heading: The key numbers
notes: The report opens on the last 14 days. Your time in range is 81%, and its target is 70% or more.

transcript.heading: Choose the period
notes: To see a longer time, open the date range at the top of the report.
Choose 30 days. The calendar shows the days it covers.
Apply, and the whole report loads again.

transcript.heading: The same page, for 30 days
notes: Every figure now covers 30 days. Your time in range is 78%, against 81% over 14 days.

transcript.heading: Time in range
notes: On an average day, that is 18 hours 46 minutes in range, 57 minutes low and 4 hours 17 minutes high.

transcript.heading: What your data tells you
notes: Over 30 days, the report finds two new patterns: time very low and time very high are above their targets.

glucose-distribution.title: Glucose Distribution
glucose-distribution.summary: How your time divides across glucose ranges.

transcript.heading: Time in each range
notes: This ring shows how your time divides across glucose ranges. The green part is the tight range, 70 to 140 mg/dL: 65% of your time.
The teal part is the rest of the target range, 140 to 180 mg/dL: 16% of your time.
To see the whole target range as one part, select Hide Tight Range.
Now one part shows all your time from 70 to 180 mg/dL: 81%. The consensus target is more than 70%.

transcript.heading: Range by hour of the day
notes: Each column is one hour of the day, split by range. From 1am to 6am, almost all of your time is in range.
9am is your hardest hour. 33.3% of it is from 180 to 250 mg/dL, and 12.5% is above 250.

heart-rate.title: Heart Rate
heart-rate.summary: Your heart rate through each day, with your glucose on the same line.

transcript.heading: Your heart rate in numbers
notes: Your average heart rate over these 14 days is 67 bpm.
Your resting estimate is 53 bpm. Only one reading in ten is lower.

transcript.heading: One row for each day
notes: The blue dots are your heart rate. At night it stays low: 52 bpm at 3 AM on Oct 18.
At 5:34 PM it climbs to 150 bpm, your highest. Your glucose stays in range, at 92 mg/dL.

transcript.heading: Go back a week
notes: The arrows move the rows a week at a time. The down arrow shows the week before.

transcript.heading: The same hour, a week before
notes: Now Oct 11 sits where Oct 18 was. A week before, your heart rate climbs to 148 bpm at almost the same time.

hourly-stats.title: Hourly Patterns
hourly-stats.summary: Every day laid over one clock, to find your best and hardest hours.

transcript.heading: At a glance
notes: Over 14 days, 9am to 10am has the least time in range: 54.2%. Its readings go mostly above range.

transcript.heading: Hour by hour
notes: Each bar is one hour. At 9am, 45.8% of your readings are above range.
Lows show at the bottom, in orange and red. At 4pm, 12.2% of your readings are below range.

transcript.heading: A longer view
notes: Two weeks can hide the real pattern. To see more, open the date range.
Choose 30 days.
Apply, and every hour is worked out again from 30 days of data.

transcript.heading: The pattern over 30 days
notes: Over 30 days the picture changes. 1pm to 2pm now has the least time in range: 52.6%.
And 3pm to 4pm has the most time below range: 13.8%. The afternoon is the hardest part of your day.

idp.title: Insulin Dosing Profile
idp.summary: Your insulin and your glucose, side by side.

transcript.heading: Glycemic Risk Index
notes: The Glycemic Risk Index puts the risk of lows and highs into one number, from 0 to 100. A lower score is better.
The dot shows where your lows and highs put you. Over 14 days your score is 25, in Zone B: 21 to 40.

transcript.heading: Your boluses
notes: Under your glucose pattern and basal rate, this chart shows how many boluses you give in each hour. Most come at breakfast: 3.7 a day at 7am.

transcript.heading: Ready for a clinic visit
notes: Before a clinic visit, set the period your care team asks for. Open the date range.
Select 30 Days. The calendar marks the days it covers.
Then select Apply Filters. The whole report loads again for 30 days.

transcript.heading: Thirty days
notes: Over 30 days your score is 29. It is still in Zone B, with highs as the larger part of your risk.

insulin-delivery.title: Insulin Delivery
insulin-delivery.summary: Your basal and bolus insulin, over 30 days.

transcript.heading: Insulin, day by day
notes: Each bar is one day. The lower part of the bar is basal insulin. The upper part is bolus insulin.
On most days you take 30 to 50 units. Over 30 days, the average is 39.9 units a day: 55% basal and 45% bolus.

transcript.heading: Insulin by hour of the day
notes: This card splits your insulin by time of day. Evening and night get the most: 14.3 units, 36% of the day.

transcript.heading: Compare the latest week
notes: Is your last week like the rest of the month? Open the date range.
Select 7 Days. The calendar marks the days it covers.
Then select Apply Filters. The report loads again for those 7 days.

transcript.heading: The last 7 days
notes: In the last 7 days your total daily dose is 37.5 units, against 39.9 over 30 days. The split stays near 56% basal and 44% bolus.

overview.title: Reports
overview.summary: Your glucose at a glance, with every report one step away.

transcript.heading: Your last 14 days
notes: 81% of your readings are in range, 70 to 180 mg/dL. The target is at least 70%.
Next to it are your key figures. Your average glucose is 135 mg/dL, and your eHbA1c is 6.3%.

transcript.heading: Your typical day
notes: The blue line is your median glucose at each hour of the day.
Your glucose is highest at 9am, with a median of 169 mg/dL.

transcript.heading: Every report
notes: Each report looks at your data in a different way. The AGP shows your typical day in full.
Hourly Patterns finds the hours of the day that go well, and the hours that are harder.
